newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE eyes more fund money in softs, agriculture.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE eyes more fund money in softs, agriculture.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) is trying to sell more of its agricultural and soft commodity products to huge futures funds, a senior LIFFE official said on Tuesday.
The exchange is frustrated by the relative ignorance of managed futures funds on soft commodities as their exposure to commodity markets mainly consists of energy and metals derivatives.

But Clive Furness, director of commodity products, said the Exchange was now planning to set up a new commodity index encompassing coffee, cocoa, sugar and wheat to enlarge the tiny slice of investment these markets have been able to muster from managed funds.

"Managed futures funds ignore soft agricultural commodities. This is something we are looking for people to come into our markets," Furness told a conference on risk management in agriculture. Fund involvement is crucial for increasing liquidity in futures as they bring the speculative money that assumes the risk that physical traders and producers want to hedge, thus making the market easier for players to get in and out.
Furness said a team of experts were analysing the correlation between metals, energy, softs and agricultural commodity prices to advise funds on asset allocation.

Commodity products, which came under the wings of LIFFE on September 16, were already benefiting from increased financial resources made available to them to chase liquidity through educational and marketing schemes.
"We set aggressive business goals. Our goal is to be the dominant factor in European agriculture products," said Furness.
He said 77 companies had so far bought the "F" shares which allow them to trade commodity products. These are still traded on a separate floor but a co-location to LIFFE premises is expected in 1998.
